name: OpenCatalogi
description: Design tokens for OpenCatalogi, transcribed from the tokens opencatalogi.nl ships
provenance: the custom properties served by opencatalogi.nl (read 2026-08-20)
_comment_source: There is no npm package for this design system, so the palette was read
off the running site: 94 --opencatalogi-* custom properties, extracted
from the stylesheets opencatalogi.nl serves on 2026-08-20.
THE VALUES ARE TRANSCRIBED IN FULL, not aliased to another set. The gray,
green, magenta, blue, red, purple and yellow ramps happen to be identical
to the Rotterdam Design System's today, and the font stack is literally
RODS' — OpenCatalogi's system is RODS-derived. Writing those as
`var(--rods-...)` would turn a fact about today into a dependency, and
the day RODS moves, this set would move with it without anyone deciding
The families below that RODS does NOT have — pink, lime-green,
soft-green, dark-blue, dark-green, dark-yellow, light-blue, brown,
dark-brown, bright-orange — are the ones that make this its own set.
_comment_ramp: The role layer addresses colour through --vng-color-* / --tilburg-color-*
names. Those are the role layer's INTERNAL vocabulary; substituting them
re-brands all 707 var()-derived component declarations at once.
Values are the palette above, restated. `from` names the palette token so
a reader can check the mapping without holding both files open.

gray-900.from: DERIVED — gray-tint-11 darkened; the ramp ends at tint-11

gray-950.from: DERIVED — gray-tint-11 darkened; the ramp ends at tint-11

blue-100.from: MEASURED — the search band background on opencatalogi.nl

blue-500.from: MEASURED — the sub-footer band and card metadata colour

red-100.from: DERIVED — red-tint-01 lightened; no notification tints in this set

red-200.from: DERIVED — red-tint-01 lightened; no notification tints in this set

_comment_literal_overrides: Colours the role layer hard-codes inside component declarations rather
than aliasing the ramp, so they have no ramp NAME to substitute on.
#004488 is deliberately KEPT: measured on opencatalogi.nl, the pagination
buttons render rgb(0, 68, 136) — the role layer's own blue, which that
site does not override either. Matching it means changing nothing.
_comment_upstream_overrides: THE LOGO IS A TOKEN, and until this was set it was not a themeable one.
--conduction-logo-*-background-image, and the shared role layer ships a VNG
mark baked into that token as a data URI. The capture from opencatalogi.nl
deliberately skips data URIs — one of them is roughly a megabyte of base64
— so the token fell through to the role layer's default and an OpenCatalogi
portal wore the VNG logo in its header AND its footer.
These are overrides rather than gap-fillers precisely because something
already defines them; the generator drops a gap-filler that shadows, which
is how the distinction earned its keep here.
Pointing them at --nldesign-logo-url makes the logo follow the token set
for EVERY brand, which is what a portal switching themes has to mean.

--denhaag-step-marker-current-color.reason: the captured #1791d4 on the current-step fill #e8f4fb is 3.11:1; the set's own blue-500 #003865 reaches 10.70:1 (denhaag-component-tokens, task 3.2)

--denhaag-step-marker-checked-color.reason: the captured #00811f on the checked-step fill #e6f3e9 is 4.41:1; the set's own green-400 #006e32 reaches 5.60:1 (denhaag-component-tokens, task 3.2)

--tilburg-erm-font-size.reason: THE CAPTURE HOISTED A DELIBERATELY-SCOPED TOKEN. On opencatalogi.nl this is undefined at `html` and 12px only inside `.ac-app-container`, so the `body, html {font-size: var(--tilburg-erm-font-size)}` rule finds nothing and the root stays 16px. Read from the container and written to `:root`, that rule DID find it and every rem on the page shrank 25% — heading-3 rendered 24px against the reference's 32px, small text 9px against 12px

--tilburg-typography-font-family-primary.value: TradeGothicCondensed18, Bolder, ArialforRotterdam, 'Arial Narrow', Arial, sans-serif
--tilburg-typography-font-family-primary.reason: captured verbatim as `TradeGothicCondensed18` with NO fallback — a licensed face this app does not serve, so every heading fell back to the browser's default SERIF

--conduction-logo-header-background-imag.reason: the role layer bakes in a VNG mark; the logo must follow the token set

--conduction-logo-footer-background-imag.reason: same VNG mark in the footer band

--conduction-logo-navbar-background-imag.reason: same VNG mark in the navbar

does not re-brand them either — it loads the same shared layer and lets
these through. Matching the reference here means changing nothing, so
each is listed with what it is rather than left in the generator's
'unmapped' warning, where ten permanent entries would train a reader to

keepLiterals.#004589: near-duplicate of #004488 in the role layer
keepLiterals.#034591: role-layer link blue, not overridden by the reference

_comment_semantic: MEASURED ON opencatalogi.nl AT 1280px, 2026-08-20 — every value below is
a computed style read off the running page, not a guess:
breadcrumb + 'Lees meer' link   rgb(0, 129, 31)   green, underlined
search submit button            rgb(201, 54, 117) magenta, radius 0
LINKS ARE GREEN AND UNDERLINED here, where Rotterdam's are black. That is
the clearest visible difference between the two sets and the reason this
is a set of its own rather than an alias of rotterdam.
_comment_component_overrides: The card family, as on rotterdam — consumed by the bundled CSS and
defined by almost no set in this repo.
The chrome bands are here too because they are what a pixel comparison
against opencatalogi.nl actually turns on, and none of them has a

typography._comment: opencatalogi.nl sets its site title in TradeGothicCondensed18, which is licensed and not redistributed here. Everything else on the page uses the stack below, and the title falls through to it.

borderRadius._comment: Square-cornered throughout — measured 0px on the textbox, the submit button, the sort select and the pagination buttons.
